question: Which of the five has been most explicit about serving mass-affluent clients, and what exactly have they said?

claims.text: Bank of America's GWIM segment is the only one of the five whose own materials use the term. In a GWIM investor-day slide (published 2025-11-05), titled "GWIM Advisor Teams Cultivate Client Relationships and Deliver the Platform's Solutions", the "Wealth Continuum" lists "Mass Affluent ($500K - $1MM)" and, next to it, "High Net Worth ($1MM - $10MM)". The slide gives a definition by asset band. The evidence has no accompanying narrative.

On the 3Q26 earnings call (published 2026-10-14), BAC CFO Alastair Borthwick said Merrill added about 4,200 net new households with at least $500,000 in assets, up 17%. He said the Private Bank added 470 net new relationships with at least $3 million under management. He said these results "reflect strong demand for advice". The $500,000 threshold matches the lower bound of the mass-affluent band on the investor-day slide, but he did not use the words "mass affluent" in this passage.

Edward Jones's 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) names its new-client targets as High Net Worth, Workplace (local business owners and their employees) and a digital platform for Next Generation investors. It does not use "mass affluent".

Morgan Stanley's 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-19) describes Wealth Management as serving "individual investors, including high and ultra-high net worth individuals, and businesses and institutions", through Advisor-Led, Self-Directed and Workplace channels. It does not use "mass affluent".

Schwab's 2Q26 deck (published 2026-07-21) cites "61%" of "Affluent clients that prefer to consolidate wealth & banking relationships". It uses "affluent", not "mass affluent", and gives no band definition.

adjacent.text: A Cerulli release (published 2026-03-25) says middle-market and mass-affluent households with $100,000 to $2 million in financial assets hold $25 trillion across 46.9 million households.
adjacent.differs_because: This is third-party research on the market, not a statement by any of the five firms about serving these clients.

adjacent.text: A trade article about Morgan Stanley (published 2026-10-21) quotes a Cerulli finding that 52% of mass-affluent participants without an advisor say their retirement account provider is their primary source of planning guidance.
adjacent.differs_because: The mass-affluent figure is Cerulli's, reported in trade press. It is indicative only and is not a Morgan Stanley statement of intent.

gaps.what: Raymond James: no statement about serving mass-affluent clients was found in the evidence provided.
gaps.suggested_source: Raymond James Private Client Group investor-day materials or earnings-call Q&A on client segments and account minimums

gaps.what: Edward Jones, Morgan Stanley and Schwab: no first-party statement using "mass affluent" was found. The evidence only shows adjacent terms (high net worth, workplace, "affluent").
gaps.suggested_source: Firm investor presentations, earnings-call transcripts or client-segment disclosures

gaps.what: Bank of America: the investor-day slide gives only a label and an asset band. Management's own explanation of how it serves the $500K–$1MM segment is not in the evidence. Merrill's standalone results are also not available.
gaps.suggested_source: Full GWIM investor-day transcript or presentation notes
